column1: # Exported symbols whose *reference* name a function-like C macro composes, and whose port name
# is this project's rename of the reference's own package identity (PORTING.md 0.1-19's name
# Column 1 is the macro's *name*, not the reference symbol: the reference's own package identity
# is read out of the reference text (the paste's prefix) and is deliberately elided here, as
# The reading (`tools/extract-abi.py`'s `substituted_exports`) accepts a port symbol only when all
# three hold: a row names the composing macro, the C file's own text (or one of the headers it
# includes) defines that macro as a paste of a prefix in front of its parameter, and that same C
# text invokes the macro with exactly the symbol's suffix.  Nothing else is exempted by this table.

column3: android.h 344's `#define NATIVE_NAME(name)` pastes the reference's own Java package in front of its argument; the class this tree loads is `org.femacs.EmacsNative`, so every JNI definition carries the renamed prefix as `#[unsafe(export_name = "Java_org_femacs_EmacsNative_<name>")]` (`docs/ports/excluded-macros.txt` 150 records the macro and the replacement; the Kotlin side is ported with the same package)
